title: FACT CHECK: Dutch ambassador’s Davao visit not about freeing Duterte from ICC
summary: Reports show that the Netherlands ambassador’s visit focused on discussions around economic ties, with no mention of the former president’s release from ICC custody

blocks.text: Claim: Former president Rodrigo Duterte is set to be released following the visit of Roderick Wols, Ambassador of the Netherlands to the Philippines, to Davao City.

Why we fact-checked this: The Facebook reel bearing the claim has already received 561,000 views, 21,300 reactions, 2,200 shares, and 1,200 comments as of writing. It was posted on November 22 and continues to gain traction up to this date.The 45-minute reel featured photos of Wols and Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte during the former’s visit to the city on November 10.Text on the video says, “Shocked ang lahat! Big surprise ito! ICC Netherlands? Netherlands pumirma sa Davao uuwi na si tatay? Baste VP Sara totoo ba?” (Everyone is shocked! This is a huge surprise! The ICC in the Netherlands? The Netherlands signed something in Davao. Is Tatay coming home? Baste, VP Sara, is this true?)

A narrator can also be heard saying, “Tila isang malaking good news at pag-asa ang hatid ng diplomatikong hakbang na ito para sa pamilya Duterte at sa posibleng paglaya ni PRRD.”(This diplomatic move appears to bring significant good news and a sense of hope for the Duterte family, as well as for the potential release of [former president Rodrigo Roa Duterte].)

The facts: Duterte is not set to be released following the Netherlands ambassador’s visit to Davao City. Reports show that the courtesy call only tackled discussions on strengthening economic ties, with no mention of the former president’s release from the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC).

The Davao City Investment Promotion Center, the local government’s investment promotion arm, wrote in a Facebook post on November 11 that the officials discussed “expanding foreign direct investments, exploring land reform dynamics, and prioritizing agricultural modernization and food security as primary avenues for Dutch capital engagement.”

The post added that Wols expressed strong enthusiasm for pitching Davao City’s investment potential in the Netherlands, noting the impact of Filipino professionals across Dutch communities.Wols’ visit was part of the celebration of the 75th anniversary of Philippines-Netherlands diplomatic relations. Before the courtesy call with Mayor Duterte, Wols delivered a lecture at the Holy Cross of Davao College on November 9.

Independent organization: The ICC is an independent international judicial institution established and governed by the Rome Statute, a multilateral treaty. Although its seat is in The Hague, Netherlands, the country serves as its host state rather than as the authority overseeing the court’s judicial proceedings.
Wols is not connected to Duterte’s case at the ICC, which is being handled by the ICC Trial Chamber III.

Duterte trial: The former president, arrested in March 2025, remains detained at the ICC facility in The Hague. He is set to face trial on November 30 for three counts of crimes against humanity related to his administration’s bloody war on drugs.
